knowledge_point.title: Calculating the Value of a Scalar

question.:question/problem:
If $kA=\begin{bmatrix}-49 & -49 & 7\end{bmatrix}$,
where $A=\begin{bmatrix}-7 & -7 & 1\end{bmatrix}$
and $k$ is a scalar, calculate the value of $k.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To express $kA,$ we multiply each entry of $A$ by $k,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}kA & =k\cdot \begin{bmatrix}-7 & -7 & 1\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}- 7 k & - 7 k & k\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set the above result equal to the matrix given for $kA$ in the problem statement:

$$
\begin{bmatrix}- 7 k & - 7 k & k\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-49 & -49 & 7\end{bmatrix}
$$

We can solve for $k$ by equating any two corresponding (nonzero) elements. Let's choose the elements in row $1$ and column $3$, $k$ and $7.$ Equating these elements, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}k & =7 \\ k & =7.\end{aligned}
$$

**Note:** We would still get the same result if we chose any other two corresponding (nonzero) elements.
